extracted.intended_audience: researchers, research funders and programme administrators, peer review policy makers, and scholars of research assessment
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis and evaluation of external peer review reports for grant proposals, including measurement of scores and investigation of factors (gender, reviewer source, affiliation, form changes) that influence those scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score (1–6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall score on a scale from 1 (worst) to 6 (best).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary outcome measure used to quantify reviewers' evaluations; reported as mean predicted values with 95% CIs. This numeric scale is the principal metric for comparing reviewer assessments across groups and over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant gender
rubrics_metrics.description: Gender of applicants influences peer review scores: 'male applicants received more favourable evaluation scores than female applicants (+0.18 points; 95% CI 0.14 to 0.23)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gender differences persisted after adjustment but were attenuated in multivariable analysis (+0.08; 95% CI 0.04 to 0.13). The paper highlights applicant gender as a potential source of bias that funders should monitor and address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer gender
rubrics_metrics.description: Gender of peer reviewers influences scoring: 'male reviewers awarded higher scores than female reviewers (+0.11; 95% CI 0.08 to 0.15)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer characteristics (including gender) can systematically affect scores and should be considered when interpreting review outcomes or designing reviewer selection/training policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source of reviewer nomination (applicant-nominated vs funder-nominated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant-nominated reviewers awarded higher scores than reviewers nominated by the SNSF (+0.53; 95% CI 0.50 to 0.56).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing applicants to nominate reviewers is associated with substantially more favourable assessments. The SNSF abandoned applicant nomination as a policy response. Recommendation: funders should consider restrictions on applicant-nominated reviewers or implement safeguards to mitigate this bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer affiliation / country (Swiss vs outside Switzerland)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers from outside of Switzerland gave more favourable scores than reviewers affiliated with Swiss institutions (+0.53; 95% CI 0.49 to 0.56).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geographic or institutional affiliation of reviewers can affect outcomes; funders should account for affiliation effects in analyses and reviewer selection to reduce systematic differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant track record emphasized by evaluation form
rubrics_metrics.description: The new evaluation form introduced in September 2011 'may inadvertently have given more emphasis to the applicant's track record.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to evaluation forms (what is asked/evaluated) can shift what reviewers weight and may increase bias. When designing forms, consider which applicant attributes (e.g., past track record) are foregrounded and how that may differentially affect groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment/control variables for fair analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses were adjusted for research topic, applicant's age, nationality, affiliation and calendar period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To assess bias in peer review fairly, statistical models should control for confounders such as research topic, applicant age, nationality, institutional affiliation and submission period. These factors are relevant covariates when estimating associations between applicant/reviewer characteristics and scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness and monitoring of bias in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review of grant applications 'might be prone to biases stemming from different applicant and reviewer characteristics.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funders and administrators should actively investigate and monitor potential biases (gender, nomination source, affiliation, form effects) in peer review processes and interpret scores with awareness of these influences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to conduct similar studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors 'encourage other funders to conduct similar studies, in order to improve the evidence base for rational and fair research funding.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A suggested operational policy: funders should periodically analyse their own peer review data to detect biases and assess the impact of procedural changes (e.g., form revisions, reviewer selection methods).
